audit.whatIsWrong: Level chart disagrees across layers: phases[3..6].side read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill while win[3..6] read Viktor/Anivia/Anivia/Anivia, and the packet chart agrees with win[].
audit.why: Two layers render two different answers to 'who wins Level 4-5'. Packet levelChart is Viktor x4 then Anivia x3.
audit.corrected: phases[3].side=Viktor, phases[4..6].side=Anivia to match win[] and the packet.

audit.why: Spikes are right in shape: Lost Chapter ends the mana war, level 6 Glacial Storm inverts wave tempo, Rylai's/Seraph's makes the storm permanent. Viktor's own spike is Hex Fragment augments plus Arcane Storm at 6 (120s at rank 1).
audit.corrected: Kept the spike structure, replaced the fabricated ability names inside it.

audit.whatIsWrong: Text calls Viktor's E 'Death Ray' and his R 'Chaos Storm' (both legacy/false names), calls Gravity Field a root, and never states the three decisive interactions.
audit.why: Riot data: E is Hextech Ray (525 range, 12/11/10/9/8s), R is Arcane Storm (120/100/80s, channel flagged interruptible), W is Gravity Field (17/16/15/14/13s) which slows and stuns only if the target lingers. Q Siphon Power is a shield plus an auto-attack reset.
audit.corrected: Use Hextech Ray and Arcane Storm. State that Flash Frost cancels the Arcane Storm channel, that Gravity Field punishes standing rather than crossing, and that Siphon Power's shield plus auto reset is the burst tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns carried no numbers and two filler lines about Anivia's own W and R.
audit.why: Real cooldowns make the advice actionable: Gravity Field 17s at rank 1, Arcane Storm 120s at rank 1.
audit.corrected: Rewrote with the real numbers and the channel-cancel interaction.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing mentioned that Arcane Storm is an interruptible channel or that Siphon Power shields the burst window.
audit.why: Both are listed in _missing for this exact matchup and both change how you time a commit.
audit.corrected: Added to spikes[1].text, breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.carry.

edits.before: Viktor wins by landing Gravity Field, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Viktor wins by chipping with Hextech Ray, stunning you in Gravity Field, then steering Arcane Storm onto the egg.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Crystallize has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Viktor Gravity Field: 17s at rank 1 — cross it, never stand in it; the stun only lands if you linger, so step up while it recharges. - Arcane Storm is 120s at rank 1 and a channel: your Flash Frost cancels it. - Siphon Power shields his burst — bait it out first.

edits.before: Carry by controlling space — storm and wall decide where fights happen, and your stun decides who dies first inside them.
edits.after: Carry by denying Viktor a stationary target — storm the ground he wants to steer Arcane Storm onto, and stun him out of the channel.

edits.before: Viktor spends Gravity Field early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Crystallize behind him: Viktor has no dash, so wall plus chill makes the gank unmissable.

edits.before: That’s Viktor’s bread-and-butter play — deny it and they run out of answers.
edits.after: Your Q costs 80 mana and is your only stun — spend it dry and his walk-up is free.

edits.before: Your wall is your Flash — a wasted Crystallize means the next gank kills the bird AND the egg.
edits.after: Hextech Ray cuts a line through minions — last-hit behind the caster wave and his 12s E hits nothing.

edits.before: Spamming Q on cooldown until you are out of mana with no stun threat left — that is when Viktor walks straight at you.
edits.after: Rebirth is your only escape — without the egg up, Gravity Field plus his jungler ends the lane, not just the wave.

edits.before: Level 1: Viktor's Death Ray poke already outranges and outdamages Anivia's non-functional early kit, giving Viktor the clear edge.
edits.after: Level 1: Viktor's Hextech Ray (E) sweeps the whole minion line for free while your Flash Frost is a slow skillshot you must save.

edits.before: Level 6: Chaos Storm still edges the fight due to its range advantage, though Anivia's own Glacial Storm begins narrowing the gap for the first time.
edits.after: Level 6: Arcane Storm still edges the fight — he steers it onto you at 700 range — though Glacial Storm finally gives you ground he cannot hold.

edits.before: Viktor's Death Ray-Gravity Field combo out-pokes your slower Q-W setup and zones you off farm without much risk to himself.
edits.after: Viktor's Hextech Ray into Gravity Field zones you off farm; the field stuns only if you linger, so cross it, never trade inside it.

edits.before: Chaos Storm still edges the fight since it out-ranges your engage, but your Glacial Storm zone starts closing the gap for the first time.
edits.after: Arcane Storm is a channel he steers, and your Flash Frost stun cancels it outright — Glacial Storm closes the gap for the first time.

edits.before: Wall-stunning him into Glacial Storm one-shots his squishy frame before Chaos Storm's zone can matter, and Rebirth buys the time to close out the trade.
edits.after: Wall-stunning him into Glacial Storm one-shots his squishy frame before Arcane Storm's zone can matter, and Rebirth buys the time to close out the trade.

edits.before: Anivia is clearly behind through level 5 — Viktor's Death Ray poke and Gravity Field zone control outrange and outpoke your unset-up combo, and he can farm and harass simultaneously with little risk. This continues to level 6, where Chaos Storm still edges the exchange, though your own ultimate starts closing the damage gap for the first time. Play patiently, farm under tower when pushed, and avoid standing in his Gravity Field — getting rooted there invites a combo you can't answer yet.
edits.after: Anivia is clearly behind through level 5 — Viktor's Hextech Ray (E) and Gravity Field zone control outpoke your unset-up combo, and he farms and harasses in one cast with little risk. This continues to level 6, where Arcane Storm still edges the exchange, though your own ultimate starts closing the damage gap for the first time. Play patiently, farm under tower when pushed, and never linger inside Gravity Field — stay in it and the stun lands a combo you can't answer yet.

edits.before: With a full combo, wall-stunning Viktor into Glacial Storm deletes his squishy frame well before his own zone control can turn the fight back his way. Rebirth is the difference-maker here — it buys the extra beat needed to finish him off even if he lands Chaos Storm first. Group around your wall in fights and force him to commit Gravity Field early; that's where Anivia's late-game combo finally wins clean.
edits.after: With a full combo, wall-stunning Viktor into Glacial Storm deletes his squishy frame well before his own zone control can turn the fight back his way. Rebirth is the difference-maker here — it buys the extra beat needed to finish him off even if he lands Arcane Storm first. Group around your wall in fights and force him to commit Gravity Field early; that's where Anivia's late-game combo finally wins clean.

edits.before: Zone Anivia off CS with Death Ray poke from max range
edits.after: Zone Anivia off CS with Hextech Ray through the wave
